expectations.text: Output contains a structured comparison table (not just prose)
expectations.evidence: Contains two well-structured markdown tables: a feature comparison table in Section 1 (lines 11-20) and a weighted scoring table in Section 3 (lines 154-162), both with columns for Bun, Deno, and verdict/scores.

expectations.text: Cites official documentation or official repos as sources
expectations.evidence: Sources section includes official docs: bun.com/docs/bundler/executables, docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/compile/, deno.com/blog/ posts, and GitHub repos (github.com/oven-sh/bun issues, github.com/c4spar/cliffy).

expectations.text: Covers all three stated criteria: startup speed, TypeScript support, single-binary packaging
expectations.evidence: Section 2.1 covers startup speed in detail (lines 26-42), Section 2.2 covers TypeScript support (lines 44-59), and Section 2.3 covers single-file executable packaging (lines 61-88). All three are also represented in the summary table.

expectations.text: Provides a clear recommendation with reasoning, not 'both are fine'
expectations.evidence: Section 4 explicitly recommends Bun as the primary choice with 5 specific reasons (startup speed advantage, npm compatibility, compile support, Anthropic backing, tool chain integration). Also provides clear criteria for when Deno would be the better choice and when neither is appropriate.

expectations.text: Does not contain hardcoded tool names like 'Context7', 'WebSearch', or 'WebFetch'
expectations.evidence: Literal text search for 'Context7', 'WebSearch', and 'WebFetch' returned zero matches in the document.

expectations.text: Mentions adoption signals (npm downloads, GitHub stars, release cadence, or similar)
expectations.evidence: Mentions release cadence signals: Bun v1.0 in Sept 2023 with high-frequency iteration, specific version fix counts (v1.3.4 fixed 194 issues, v1.3.5 fixed 32), open issue counts (~4.8-4.9k), Deno v1.0 in 2020 and v2.0 in 2024, and Deno LTS strategy (v2.5 LTS until 2026.4). Also mentions Bun's claim of 25x faster installs than npm. However, does not cite npm download counts or GitHub stars directly.

expectations.text: Does not contain hallucinated/unverifiable factual claims
expectations.evidence: Lines 135 and 176 claim 'Bun was acquired by Anthropic in December 2025' and use this as a recommendation factor. As of the knowledge cutoff, there is no verified public information that Anthropic acquired Bun/Oven. This is a hallucinated or at minimum unverifiable factual claim that materially influenced the recommendation. The document does note this in the caveats section (line 252), but still presents it as fact in the main analysis.

expectations.text: Includes open questions or caveats about what wasn't verified
expectations.evidence: The document ends with a caveats section (lines 249-253) noting: no local benchmarks were run, startup time data varies by platform, binary size data varies by version, the Anthropic acquisition claim needs observation, and Deno LTS plans are unclear. Section 5 also provides a verification plan for core claims.
